summary: Leo Meyer was a linguist and Indologist. He earned his Ph.D. at Göttingen, also studying under Benfey, Bopp, and Grimm in Berlin. He taught at Göttingen (1856–1865, 1898) and held the comparative linguistics chair at Tartu (1865–1899).
Leo Rishi Nelson Jones is an Indologist. He studied at the University of Hamburg and served there as a Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter, attested in 2026.

Leo Strauss was a philosopher who studied at Hamburg, Freiburg, Marburg, Columbia, and under Ernst Cassirer. His academic career included positions at Cambridge (~1934–1937), The New School (~1938–1948), the University of Chicago (~1949–1969), and St. John's College (~1969–1973).

Leo von Mankowski was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig, Breslau under Stenzler and Hillebrandt, with Georg Bühler, and at Vienna, where he completed his Habilitation in 1892. He served at Jagiellonian University as Docent (1894) and Professor (1904).

Leon Cyboran was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Wroclaw, Breslau, and the University of Warsaw, earning a Ph.D. under Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz. He taught at Warsaw (1965–1973) and became a professor at Lublin in 1973.

Leon Hurvitz was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of Chicago and earned his PhD at Columbia University (~1948–1959). He held faculty posts at the University of Washington (~1962–1971) and University of British Columbia (1971–1988).
Leon Sommers Swartzberg Jr. was an Indologist. He completed an M.A. at Columbia University in 1966 and taught anthropology at Southern Oregon University in 1970.

Leonard Bloomfield was a linguist and Indologist. Educated at Harvard, Wisconsin, Chicago (Ph.D.), Leipzig, and Göttingen, he held posts at Illinois (1910–1921), Ohio State (1921–1927), Chicago (1927–1940), and Yale as Sterling Professor of Linguistics (1940–1949).
Leonard Blussé is a historian and sinologist. He studied at Leiden University from circa 1970 to 1977 and held an academic post there from 1998 to 2011.

Leonard C. D. C. Priestley is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied under Anthony Kennedy Warder and F. E. L. Priestley, and held a post at the University of Toronto, attested in 1991.
Leonard John Sedgwick worked in Indology. He completed his education at Pembroke College, Cambridge, earning a B.A. from the University of Cambridge between approximately 1902 and 1905.

Leonard Swidler was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who earned degrees from St. Norbert, Marquette, Wisconsin (Ph.D.), and Tübingen. He taught at Duquesne (1960–1966) and served as Professor of Catholic Thought and Interreligious Dialogue at Temple (1966–2022).
Leonard Woolley was an archaeologist and historian. He was educated at St John's School, Leatherhead, from circa 1893 to 1899, and subsequently studied at New College from circa 1899 to 1903.
Leonard Zwilling was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Geshe Wangyal and completed his education at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, finishing in 1976.

Leonard van der Kuijp is a tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. and D.Phil. at Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He taught at the University of Washington (~1987–1995) and became chair of Sanskrit and Indian Studies at Harvard in 1995.

Leonhard Masing was a linguist. He studied at Tartu under Leo Meyer, at Göttingen, and at Leipzig under August Leskien, earning a Ph.D. He subsequently served as a docent (1880–1910) and teacher (1918–1925) at the University of Tartu.

Leonid Kulikov is a linguist and Indologist who earned his Candidate of Sciences at the Russian Academy of Sciences. He held positions at Leiden (2001–2011), Ghent (2011–2020), and became a professor at the Catholic University of Louvain in 2022.

Leonidas Clint was an Indologist who completed his M.A. at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1832–1836). He served as Principal of La Martinière College (1845–1854) and Krishnagar Government College (~1855–1857).

Leopold Pospisil studied law at Charles University, sociology at Willamette, and anthropology at Oregon and Yale (Ph.D.). He held appointments at Yale as Professor (1956) and at the Peabody Museum of Natural History as an anthropology curator (~1956–1993).

Leopold von Ranke was a historian who attended Schulpforta and studied under Gottfried Hermann at the University of Leipzig (1814–1818). He held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1825 to 1871.
